lis.profile: Lis — a cool, deadpan, ironic street narrator of an adult comedy show about used-car flippers. Low calm voice, dry humor, confident.
lis.notes: Part 18 of a comedy mini-series about Tolyan building his own car dealership: first buyer, a grandpa on the test drive, a deal with a jar of pickles. Brisk, ironic narration. Last line: a confident, warm advertising pitch for the bot «Перехват».

tolyan.profile: Tolyan — a cocky Russian used-car flipper (perekup) in his 30s, street swagger, deep raspy voice, show-off, calls everyone «брат». Adult street comedy.
tolyan.notes: No swearing. Line 1: calm, confident, a little smug. Line 2: excited, quick, on a video call.

palych.profile: Palych — an old Russian grandpa in his 70s, retired driver, owner of a perfectly kept old Lada; grumpy, suspicious of car flippers, kind underneath.
palych.notes: No swearing. Line 1: protective, firm. Line 2: loud, bossy, from the back seat, comic. Line 3: sly bargaining, generous.

rimma.profile: Rimma Zakharovna — a strict, businesslike Russian woman in her 50s who owns a former gas station lot; cool, precise, a little ironic, always calls Tolyan by his full name «Анатолий».
rimma.notes: One line: dry, ironic, counting cars.

leha.profile: Lyokha — the most serious car dealer in Moscow: bald, tattooed, leather jacket, drives a Rolls-Royce. Low, heavy, calm, unhurried voice; speaks in short confident sentences like a mentor; dry humor.
leha.notes: No swearing. One line on a video call from his Rolls-Royce: calm, decisive, business-like.

zhora.profile: Zhora — a brash, cocky veteran Russian used-car flipper in his 50s, leather jacket, mustache, gold chain; loud, fast, mocking, calls the young rival «студент». Adult street comedy.
zhora.notes: No swearing. One line: watching through binoculars, jealous, quiet and sly, then a threatening grin.

gosha.profile: Gosha — a young Russian IT guy in his late 20s buying his first car: polite, a bit nervous, then excited.
gosha.notes: Line 1: polite, hopeful. Line 2: excited but trying to bargain. Line 3: happy, quick.
